root_causes.description: The recommendation service consumes an anomalous amount of CPU during the incident window (mean 2.343 cores, p95 3.604, peak 3.608), ~33x higher than frontend (0.070) and ~94x higher than product-catalog (0.025). Error rate, memory usage and pod restarts remain at baseline, the exact signature of an injected CPU-stress fault rather than a crash, latency, memory or dependency failure.

evidence.expected_baseline: container CPU ~0.025-0.070 cores (product-catalog 0.025, frontend 0.070, ad 0.003 during same window)
error_rate < 0.01 (confirms no http_abort or dependency failure)

evidence.observed_value: mean=105.86 MB, p50=108.95 MB, max=108.97 MB (stable, no growth)

root_causes.description: frontend is the direct upstream caller of recommendation and would surface downstream degradation, but its CPU and error rate remain at baseline, so it is not the fault origin.
product-catalog is a downstream dependency of recommendation; its CPU stays at baseline, indicating the recommendation CPU load is not caused by increased downstream dependency work.

remediation_steps: Confirm the CPU saturation source on the recommendation pod: kubectl top pods -n otel-demo and inspect for a stress-ng / busy-loop sidecar or injected fault marked seed42.
If the fault is injected, stop/disable the CPU-stress experiment targeting the recommendation service (remove the chaos/fault injection).
Verify CPU throttling on the recommendation pod (container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total) and confirm CPU returns to baseline (~0.03-0.07 cores) after the fault is removed.
Confirm frontend recommendation-call latency recovers once recommendation CPU normalizes; no pod restart is required since restarts=0.
